title: Candidate model card (v1)
description: A declarative, versioned description of one routing candidate (design.md §9.2, ADR-0003). A candidate is an execution identity, not a model ID: the same base model reached through two providers is two separate cards with two separate `id` values, because it may differ in latency, pricing, cache behavior, tool-call reliability, limits, and safety filtering (design.md §9.1). This schema describes the *curated model card* layer only. The six-level precedence chain (hard operator policy > live health > measured candidate statistics > curated model card > registry metadata > conservative unknown defaults) is a merge-time contract implemented in Phase 3, not a schema constraint (design.md §9.3, ADR-0003). Cards are untrusted input and must be schema-validated on load. A card never contains a credential value — only an environment-variable reference.

id.description: Stable candidate identifier. This is the value that appears in RouteDecision `ranked[].candidate`, `excluded[].candidate`, and `selected`, and in outcome-event `candidate`.

enabled.description: Whether this candidate participates in routing at all. A disabled card is loaded and validated but never scored.

transport.description: How the candidate is reached. Only `adapter`, `provider`, and `model` are required. ADR-0003's seven-element candidate identity (provider, endpoint, model, credential scope, protocol adapter, harness profile, harness version) is the *runtime composition* of identity performed in Phase 3 from this card plus resolved configuration — it is deliberately not the set of required card fields, because endpoint and credential scope are frequently supplied by operator configuration rather than restated per card.

adapter.description: Protocol adapter that speaks to this endpoint, e.g. `openai_compatible`, `openrouter`, `litellm` (design.md §10.1, §10.2).

provider.description: Provider identity. Part of candidate identity: the same `model` through two providers is two candidates.

base_url.description: Endpoint base URL when it is not implied by the adapter, e.g. a local Ollama, vLLM, or LM Studio server.

credential_ref.description: Reference to the credential, never the credential itself. Only an environment-variable reference (`env:NAME`) or the literal `none` for an unauthenticated local endpoint validates. This pattern is the structural guarantee that a raw API key can never be written into a card and pass validation.

capabilities.description: The eight capability dimensions from design.md §7.2, each normalized to [0, 1]. All eight are required on a card — unlike the RouteDecision requirement vector, which may be sparse. A card must be complete because a missing dimension would be read as an unconstrained surplus and silently inflate the candidate's fit.

affinities.description: Per-domain affinity scores over the ten domain tags from design.md §7.2, each normalized to [0, 1]. Domain tags are kept separate from capability scores rather than collapsed into them. Every tag is optional — an absent tag means no measured affinity — but unknown tag names fail validation, so a misspelled domain fails loudly instead of silently scoring zero.

limits.description: Hard capability limits used by the eligibility filter (design.md §7.3, §9.2). A text-only candidate — `vision: false` with `capabilities.multimodal_reasoning: 0.0` — is a normal, valid card.

context_tokens.description: Maximum total context window in tokens.

tools.description: Whether the candidate supports tool calling.

vision.description: Whether the candidate accepts image input.

structured_output.description: Whether the candidate supports schema-constrained structured output.

economics.description: Per-million-token pricing in USD. Every price is nullable, and null is semantically distinct from 0: null means the price is UNKNOWN, and unknown pricing is NEVER treated as zero cost (design.md §7.5, ADR-0003). Zero-cost defaults would make the cheapest candidate always be the one we know least about, inverting the intended behavior. An unknown-priced candidate is excluded from `economy` mode by default and permitted in `quality` only when the user explicitly allows unknown-cost models. These fields deliberately carry no `default`, so a missing price stays an explicit unknown handled by mode policy rather than being filled in by the validator.

input_per_million.description: USD per million uncached input tokens. Null means unknown, never zero.

output_per_million.description: USD per million output tokens. Null means unknown, never zero.

cache_read_per_million.description: USD per million cache-read tokens. Null means unknown, never zero.

cache_write_per_million.description: USD per million cache-write tokens. Null means unknown, never zero.

request_fee.description: Provider-specific fixed per-request fee in USD (`F_request` in design.md §7.5). Null means unknown, never zero.

harness.description: The model-specific harness profile applied when executing this candidate (design.md §10.3). Harness version is part of candidate identity per ADR-0003, so changing the harness invalidates measurements taken under the old one; `version` is therefore required whenever this block is present, and is a monotonically incrementing integer rather than a free-form string so that ordering is total and machine-checkable.

version.description: Harness profile version. Part of candidate identity — it must increment when the harness changes.

reasoning_policy.description: Reasoning-effort policy applied to this candidate, e.g. `adaptive`.

policy.description: Operator policy classifications for this candidate (design.md §7.2, §7.3, §9.2). Hard operator policy sits at the top of the precedence chain, so nothing below it — including any learned component — can restore a candidate that policy excluded.

privacy_class.description: Privacy class, matched against the request's `privacy_requirement` (cloud_allowed / approved_only / local_only) in design.md §7.2.

experimental.description: Whether the candidate is experimental and therefore held out of default routing.

allowed_modes.description: Routing modes in which this candidate may be selected. Absent means all modes.

evidence.description: Provenance for the scores on this card (design.md §9.2, ADR-0003). `source_version` is what a RouteDecision records in `model_card_version` so a decision can be replayed against the exact card snapshot that produced it, and a regression attributed to a specific card revision.

source_version.description: Version identifier of this card revision.

calibration_dataset.description: Name of the dataset the capability and affinity scores were calibrated against.

sample_count.description: Number of calibration samples behind these scores. 0 means the scores are unmeasured judgments.

context_anchor.description: Marks this candidate as a context-anchor candidate that must support the advertised virtual context window (design.md §9.4). Setup and doctor commands require at least one enabled context-anchor candidate.
